Detection of spatial co-expression modules

Source: vignettes/spatial_coexpression_modules.Rmd
spatial_coexpression_modules.Rmd

Spatially variable genes often share a pattern: genes of one cell type or tissue region rise and fall together across the section. A spatial co-expression module is such a group. spatialCoexpression() finds them in one step:

  1. each cell’s expression is averaged with its neighbours’ in a spatial network, which keeps the spatial pattern and smooths out cell-to-cell noise;
  2. the genes are correlated on the smoothed values;
  3. the correlation is clustered into modules;
  4. each module gets one score per cell, the mean expression of its genes.

The same command runs on disk-backed (GiottoDisk) objects; see Detection of spatially variable genes.

1 Setup and load example dataset 

# Ensure Giotto Suite is installed
if (!"Giotto" %in% installed.packages()) {
  pak::pkg_install("giotto-suite/Giotto")
}
# Ensure Giotto Data is installed
if (!"GiottoData" %in% installed.packages()) {
  pak::pkg_install("giotto-suite/GiottoData")
}
library(Giotto)
g <- GiottoData::loadGiottoMini("visium")

2 Select spatially variable genes

Modules are built from genes that are spatial to begin with. Rank the genes with binSpect’s join-count test and keep the top 100 (see Detection of spatially variable genes for the methods):

ranktest <- spatialAutoCor(g,
  method = "binspect",
  spatial_network_name = "spatial_network",
  return_gobject = FALSE
)
spatial_genes <- ranktest$feats[1:100]

3 Find the modules 

g <- spatialCoexpression(g,
  feats = spatial_genes,
  spatial_network_name = "spatial_network",
  n_modules = 5
)

Each gene’s module is now in the feature metadata, with spatial_module_cor, its mean correlation with the rest of its module (how firmly it belongs):

modules <- fDataDT(g)[!is.na(spatial_module),
  .(feat_ID, spatial_module, spatial_module_cor)]
head(modules[order(spatial_module, -spatial_module_cor)], 8)
##    feat_ID spatial_module spatial_module_cor
##     <char>          <int>              <num>
## 1:   Shox2              1          0.8094911
## 2:   Rgs16              1          0.8081125
## 3:    Lef1              1          0.8029107
## 4:  Synpo2              1          0.7969906
## 5: Slc17a6              1          0.7967425
## 6:   Ntng1              1          0.7924487
## 7:    Grm4              1          0.7892326
## 8:  Amotl1              1          0.7878026

smoothing sets how much a cell’s neighbours count (by default about as much as the cell itself), and smoothing = 0 correlates the unsmoothed values.

4 Inspect the modules

With return_gobject = FALSE the command returns the correlation matrix, the modules and a summary per module instead:

coexpr <- spatialCoexpression(g,
  feats = spatial_genes,
  spatial_network_name = "spatial_network",
  n_modules = 5,
  return_gobject = FALSE
)
coexpr$summary
##    module  size within_cor between_cor     score
##     <int> <int>      <num>       <num>     <num>
## 1:      1    39  0.7149600 -0.31448533 0.7149600
## 2:      3     4  0.8421133 -0.12399741 0.6817009
## 3:      4    20  0.7310168 -0.08401100 0.5625362
## 4:      5    22  0.7196101 -0.05392370 0.5321073
## 5:      2    15  0.3621740 -0.09061745 0.2810949

within_cor is the mean correlation between a module’s genes and between_cor their mean correlation with the other modules; score ranks the coherent, distinct modules first.

heatmapCoexpression(g, coexpr)

5 Module scores in the tissue

The module scores are stored as the spatial enrichment spatial_module:

spatCellPlot(g,
  spat_enr_names = "spatial_module",
  cell_annotation_values = as.character(coexpr$summary$module),
  point_size = 2,
  cow_n_col = 2
)

6 Top genes per module

For downstream analyses such as spatially informed clusters or spatial domains with HMRF, take the genes that belong most firmly to each module. In a full-size dataset, about 30 genes per module is a common choice.

top_genes <- fDataDT(g)[!is.na(spatial_module)][
  order(-spatial_module_cor), head(.SD, 10), by = spatial_module]
spatial_genes <- top_genes$feat_ID
